This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let\[f(n) = \min_{i<n} (p_{n+i}+p_{n-i}),\]where $p_k$ is the $k$th prime. Is it true that\[\limsup_n (f(n)-2p_n)=\infty?\]
#454: [ErGr80,p.90]
number theory | 
primes
Pomerance [Po79] has proved the $\limsup$ is at least $2$.

 This looks hard, even if one assumes powerful conjectures such as the prime tuples conjecture. The key values of $n$ which would contribute to this lim sup are the extreme points of the convex hull of the graph $\{ (n,p_n): n \in {\mathbf N} \}$ of the primes, but this is expected to be a very sparse set and so even the prime tuples conjecture doesn't tell us much about what happens near those points.
 TerenceTao
